appearance_facts.fact: Five blue circular markers are arranged in a steep upward diagonal, with each higher-spending region also higher in sales.
Region E is the highest and rightmost point, clearly separated from Region D.
Region A is the lowest and leftmost point.
Regions B, C, and D lie between A and E in a roughly evenly spaced ascending line.
Each marker has a black text label naming its region.

printed_facts.fact: Title reads “Top Regions: Ad Spend vs Sales”.
Y-axis is labeled “Sales ($ thousands)” with ticks from 50 to 160 in increments of 10.
X-axis is labeled “Advertising Spend ($ thousands)” with ticks from 25 to 75 in increments of 5.
Labels read Region A, Region B, Region C, Region D, and Region E.
Approximate plotted coordinates: A (30, 58), B (40, 66), C (50, 81), D (60, 106), E (70, 151).

public_definitions: The task asks to review the regional spend and sales dashboard, then choose the spend-increase decision.

The primary field is “Budget Approval Decision” with options: “Hold recommendation and request full regional spend-sales analysis”, “Approve broader region-wide spend increase”, and “Approve a limited pilot increase for selected regions only”.
uncertain: No legend, threshold line, or policy table is shown, so the decision rule linking the scatter pattern to a specific option is not printed on the page.
